step1_summary.Chief complaint: Lip swelling developing after eating prawn soup
Symptoms: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating prawn soup
Swelling is progressive and worsening on upper lip, especially left corner
Difficulty breathing and feeling throat closing up
Past similar episode about a year ago after eating curry, with swelling and breathing difficulty
Past medical history: Previously required an injection (likely epinephrine) as a child for severe allergic reaction
Medications/allergies: Unclear if current antihistamines regularly used
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: Patient reports dizziness, worsening lip swelling, feeling of throat closing and breathing difficulty - no measured vital signs available

V: Angioedema due to hereditary or acquired vascular causes: could cause lip swelling and airway compromise, though typically not food-triggered
I: Allergic (IgE-mediated) reaction to prawn (shellfish) exposure causing anaphylaxis and angioedema: Lip swelling, airway symptoms, history of allergic reactions supports this
I2: Medication-induced allergic reaction (e.g., from food additives or cross reaction with known allergy medication) - less likely without new meds
C: Hereditary angioedema (C1 esterase deficiency): causes recurrent swelling but usually no urticaria and no clear food trigger in this case
A: IgE-mediated allergic reaction causing anaphylaxis and angioedema: food allergy to prawns and history of peanut allergy with previous anaphylaxis

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Anaphylaxis due to IgE-mediated allergic reaction to shellfish (prawn)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Rapidly progressive lip swelling following ingestion of prawn, associated airway symptoms (throat tightness, breathing difficulty), history of peanut allergy and previous anaphylaxis, and absence of alternative causes strongly suggest anaphylaxis.
supporting_evidence: Lip swelling started within 30 minutes after eating prawn soup
Progressive worsening of swelling with airway symptoms
History of peanut allergy and prior severe allergic reaction requiring injection
Current symptoms of difficulty breathing and dizziness

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Recurrent angioedema with airway compromise is possible, but food triggers and history of IgE allergy favor anaphylaxis. No mention of family history or typical triggers for hereditary angioedema.
opposing_evidence: Food ingestion triggering symptoms (prawn) more characteristic of allergic reaction
History of peanut allergy and previous anaphylaxis supportive of allergic etiology

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Asthma exacerbation with associated laryngeal edema
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient has asthma and difficulty breathing but lip swelling and rapid progression with clear food trigger points more to anaphylaxis than an asthma exacerbation alone.
opposing_evidence: Lip swelling and rapid facial signs more typical of allergic reaction
